theAcquisitionProcessNeverReceives.note: Every entry is false. Enforced by construction in the staging step, asserted by the freeze script, and tested in src/fixtures/eval/issue-149-acquisition-isolation.test.ts.

scanBeforeFreeze.scope: the acquisition input, the staged directory listing, the mounted file set, and every file under raw/<run>/ — as scanned FROM INSIDE the isolated boundary
scansFor: the forbidden evidence key inventory, in every emitted file
doesNotScanFor: governed Brand strings appearing inside OCR transcripts or candidate values
scanBeforeFreeze.whyNot: A legitimate OCR transcript may naturally contain the Brand text. Such text is EVIDENCE, not proof of truth leakage. Comparing emitted evidence against governed Brand strings before the freeze would misclassify a correct reading as a leak, and would require opening a truth file before the truth boundary. Truth-string inventory and comparison belong to post-freeze evaluation only.
scanBeforeFreeze.hardFailure: any scanned-for item present halts with TRUTH_ISOLATION_FAILURE
scanBeforeFreeze.movedToPhase3Why: The isolated runtime cannot scan for an inventory it does not hold, and handing it that inventory would itself be the leak. Those checks run read-only, after sealing, outside the boundary.

permitted: load the post-freeze id map to attach historical case identity
load governed truth to rederive the previously carried determinations
inventory and compare truth strings against the acquired evidence
compare the new current-base snapshot with the older evidence artifact
forbidden: reordering, re-emitting or reformatting any frozen raw file

opaqueIdentity.assignmentOrder: ascending source-image SHA-256, so the sequence is deterministic and carries no ordering signal from the historical names
opaqueIdentity.stagedFilename: item-NNNN.<ext>, generic and derived only from the opaque id and the original extension

trustedStagingStep.why: Something must know which historical image becomes which opaque id, because something must copy it.

stage1TestsAre.kind: static manifest, path and import validation
stage1TestsAre.why: The Stage 1 tests read committed planning artifacts and assert their shape. They cannot demonstrate that a future process is unable to read the repository checkout.
stage1TestsAre.actualIsolationGate: a mandatory discover-mode gate inside the runtime boundary; see acquisition-runtime-isolation-contract.json

truthBoundaryChronology.supersededClaim: Both runs complete, and both raw-evidence manifests are written and hashed, BEFORE the post-freeze id map or any governed truth file is opened.
truthBoundaryChronology.whyItWasFalse: Trusted staging necessarily opens the evaluation manifest and the historical identities in order to freeze the corpus, assign opaque ids and write the post-freeze map. That happens BEFORE acquisition, so no component could truthfully claim nothing had opened them before the runs. The invariant that matters was never global ordering; it is who receives what.

onlyInOrderTo: verify source-image SHA-256 and byte size

phase2IsolatedAcquisition.cannotScanFor: historical case IDs and historical fixture paths, because it does not hold that inventory — and giving it the inventory would be the leak it is meant to prevent
phase2IsolatedAcquisition.writesAndSeals: each raw manifest inside the isolated boundary

phase3ReadOnlyIdentityLeakVerification.why: The exact historical case-ID and fixture-path inventory cannot be placed inside the acquisition runtime merely so it can scan for itself. The scan therefore runs OUTSIDE, against evidence that is already frozen.
mayRead: the historical case-ID and fixture-path inventory
does: scan the already-frozen bytes for historical case IDs
scan them for historical fixture paths
verify both raw manifests still match the bytes
mayNot: rewrite, reformat or re-emit any raw file

phase4PostFreezeEvaluation.runsAfter: phase 3 reports clean and the raw evidence is committed

forbiddenEvidenceKeyInventory.singleSourceRule: This is the ONE inventory. No contract, test or executable module may declare a second list. Amendment 5 left three different sets in play — ten keys in evidence-schema.json, seven in truth-isolation-plan.json and the scanner, five in raw-ocr-contract.json — so brandPresent, historicalCaseId and historicalImagePath were absent from the executable scanner.
forbiddenEvidenceKeyInventory.fieldNamesVersusValues: These are FIELD NAMES, prohibited inside acquisition output. The historical identifier and fixture-path VALUES are a separate matter: they are checked after sealing by the read-only identity-leak verifier, which holds an inventory the isolated runtime never receives.
forbiddenEvidenceKeyInventory.governsEveryEmittedFile: pass records, candidate records, selection records, item-level failure records, count records, manifests and provenance records alike — closed pass and candidate schemas cover two of those shapes, not all of them
